finding: On the tweets-hindi VALIDATION split (official UMSAB 'hindi' validation file, n=322 after dedup) every model scores near chance, much lower than on the same source's test split.
inconclusive_probe: Training a char-TF-IDF model on the 322 validation rows vs on 322 random train rows gives the same near-chance test macro-F1 (0.341 vs 0.347): with so few rows this probe cannot separate label noise from a harder split.
status: NOT VERIFIED. Possible causes: label/text misalignment in the source validation file, or a distribution shift. Needs manual inspection of a sample of validation tweets against their labels.
consequence: Validation-based selection on Hinglish is effectively driven by the youtube-hinglish subset. Any tweets-hindi validation number should not be used for model selection until resolved.
